description: Lens is a self-hosted archive for recordings, transcripts and documents: it transcribes, indexes and publishes them, and people search and chat over them. One operator (the instance admin) runs an instance for their own people: a FastAPI API, a Next.js web app that proxies the API and holds the sign-in session, and background workers, around one SurrealDB database, with content split into namespaces and per-namespace roles. Exposing an instance to the internet behind HTTPS (reverse proxy or Cloudflare tunnel) is supported. Only the instance admin (equivalent to host code execution) and the host operator are trusted; everyone else is trusted only as far as their role.

trust_boundaries.boundary: B1, network to web app: everything a browser, app or agent sends is untrusted; the web app forwards /api, /mcp, /iiif, /embed and /s to the API, which authorizes every call.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a browser request and changes what the API decides or what another person's browser runs

trust_boundaries.boundary: B2, request to role: the API turns a bearer token, signed link, share link, IIIF cookie or vouched-for address into a role per namespace.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable with no account, or with an account, and yields a session, token or admin the attacker was not given; setup-code findings apply only while no account exists

trust_boundaries.boundary: B2, request to role: the main boundary; namespace isolation lives here, in application code. B5: workers, the API and the web app trust the database and each other.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: lets a principal read or change more than its role and the recording's access level allow, or open media without a link the server signed for it

trust_boundaries.boundary: B4, Lens to the outside: fetches whose URL a non-admin sets, and iCal feeds, go through netguard; other admin-set URLs do not; the telemetry endpoint is only shape-checked (P-ADMIN-GUARD).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: a URL a non-admin sets, or a guarded admin operand, reaches a non-public address; or a stored secret reaches anyone but the host the admin set

trust_boundaries.boundary: B3, content to parser: uploaded and fetched bytes cross into ffmpeg, LibreOffice, Chromium, poppler and Tesseract.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from bytes an editor uploads or a watched source delivers, and the fault is in how Lens runs the tool (arguments, environment, timeouts, sandbox flags)

trust_boundaries.boundary: B2, request to role: query text from a non-admin is untrusted and runs only over the caller's readable namespaces.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: query text from a non-admin reads outside the caller's namespaces, writes, fetches, or reaches SurrealQL

trust_boundaries.boundary: B3, content to parser: uploaded and fetched bytes cross into the LLM prompt; B2 bounds the tools to the person's role.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: a non-admin (or content steering the model for one) exceeds the person's reads, changes data without approval outside notes and admin setup, or runs code on the host

trust_boundaries.boundary: B6, devices: sensor listeners take traffic from the LAN (or wider, per sensors.bind) once an admin enables them.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: the service is turned on by an admin, and the attacker lacks the login, network or token the feature requires

assumes: Host is Linux containers, an LXC on Proxmox, a NAS package, or a native install on Linux or macOS; the host and its root user are trusted.
One SurrealDB database holds every namespace, with optimistic, retried transactions; the embedded engine is for trying Lens and small archives.
Expiry uses wall-clock time with no skew handling.
Several API processes and workers may run at once; throttle counters and the setup code live in each process's memory.
Child processes (rclone, ffmpeg, LibreOffice, Chromium, Tesseract, poppler, cloudflared, llama-server, code tools, uv/pip) run as argument lists.
Listening sockets: API and web app; a loopback netguard proxy during captures; MQTT 1883 and syslog 5514 when sensors are on; llama-server when enabled.
Files live under data_dir, including secret.key when ARCHIVE_SECRET_KEY is unset; the server log carries the setup code and, without mail, sign-in links.
does_not: make outbound connections except to configured sources, model servers, mail, notification and telemetry targets, components.auto installs and model downloads, and the llama.cpp/cloudflared/hf: downloads when those features are on

properties_provided.conditions: a principal with no role in a namespace and no grant for a recording cannot read or change anything in it, except what the recording's access level opens to anyone (P-ACCESS-PARTS); the namespace and its recordings answer 404; grants for one recording open only that recording's visitor pages and IIIF
properties_provided.source: SECURITY.md "reading or changing anything in a namespace you have no role in"

properties_provided.conditions: a closed part of a public recording, and any restricted or private recording, opens only for a role, permission, IP group or link; a closed transcript's text stays out of search and downloads; only owners change access and open parts
properties_provided.source: docs/access.md "the parts of a public recording anyone may use"

properties_provided.conditions: a principal does no more than its role allows; writes need a write-capable principal and editor or owner; publishing and access changes need owner, through every API path
properties_provided.source: SECURITY.md "doing more than your role allows"

properties_provided.conditions: request text does not inject into database queries, a shell or the processing tools

properties_provided.conditions: media, frames, documents and reports open without a session only through a link the server signed for that path, or a live share link; text people or models write is never signed
a share link opens one recording, read-only; it expires and can be revoked; only hashes are stored; a dead link answers the same 410 whatever went wrong
properties_provided.source: docs/authentication.md "give read-only access to one recording's player and embed"

properties_provided.conditions: a request is authenticated only if its bearer verifies and the account and session are live; sign-out and disabling take effect at once, for every token kind; revoking an app grant or API token ends its tokens at once
properties_provided.source: docs/authentication.md "Every request checks that the account is still active"

properties_provided.conditions: /api/v1 takes bearer tokens only, never cookies; the IIIF authorization flow and the web app's NextAuth handlers are the cookie surfaces
properties_provided.source: docs/architecture.md "so there is no CSRF surface"

properties_provided.conditions: no public sign-up; only the one-time setup code makes the first admin, and it dies once an account exists
properties_provided.source: docs/configuration.md "so a stranger who finds a new"

properties_provided.conditions: sign-in links, WebAuthn flows, sign-in tickets, OAuth codes and external-login states work once; a refused or failed attempt consumes nothing

a rotated web refresh token replayed after 60 s ends the whole session; a rotated OAuth refresh token replayed within 60 s is refused and changes nothing, after that it ends the grant; a spent OAuth code replayed ends the grant
properties_provided.source: docs/authentication.md "A swapped one that comes back within 60 seconds is refused"

properties_provided.conditions: access JWT 900 s; sign-in link 72 h, emailed links 60 min; OAuth code 5 min; app tokens 60 min / 30 days; API tokens default 90 days, never past tokens.max_days

PKCE (S256) required; redirects must match a registered URI; addresses with a user name or backslash refused; the consent page cannot be framed; app tokens act as the person and never administer; /mcp refuses a token issued for another server, caps bodies at 1 MB and batches at 20
with passwords off, password sign-in, changes and resets answer 403
failed password sign-ins are throttled per email and address (8 per 15 minutes); unknown emails take as long to reject as wrong passwords; in both compose files each visitor gets their own throttle

an address opens an IP group only when the server can vouch for it, through server.trusted_proxies or LENS_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOSTS; both compose files trust the web app container so IP groups see real addresses; elsewhere a reverse proxy must set X-Forwarded-For (other variants: Q2)
properties_provided.source: docs/access.md "An address the server can't vouch for opens nothing"

properties_provided.conditions: the Host header must be a served host; this stops DNS rebinding
the API sends a strict CSP; only the player (/embed/<id>, /s/<code>) can be framed, and only by server.embed_frame_ancestors

in the compose files the database, API and Fedora ports bind to 127.0.0.1, containers run non-root with no-new-privileges, and the web app sends nosniff, a referrer policy, a permissions policy and a frame policy (HSTS through Cloudflare); in docker-compose.prod.yml the DB password is random and the web app listens on this machine unless LENS_BIND is set

stored secrets (source credentials, notification secrets, model API keys, iCal addresses) are encrypted and write-only; the API reports whether one is set, never its value; a key from the environment is never shown; they do not leak through the API, logs, exports, or a redirect to another server
properties_provided.source: SECURITY.md "stored credentials for sources and model servers leaking"

properties_provided.conditions: URLs a non-admin sets (web import and extension http tools by editors; notification targets by owners) reach public addresses only, or networks the operator listed; web paths use ports 80 and 443, follow redirects only to http and https, re-check every redirect and sub-request, and connect to the checked address

guards Lens documents on admin-set operands hold: iCal feeds are fetched like web captures (public addresses only and documents.web_networks, ports 80 and 443, the password never goes on to a server the calendar redirects to); the telemetry endpoint cannot carry a user name or password or be a link-local address

properties_provided.conditions: assistant tools that change data wait for the person's approval, except notes and an admin's setup conversation

properties_provided.conditions: no non-admin can run code on the host (owners, editors, viewers, API tokens, MCP agents, OAuth apps and model tool calls acting for one); Python tools are written by admins only and run only while an admin owns them

properties_provided.conditions: each notification event is claimed once across processes and retried with backoff
collections nest at most 8 deep, without cycles, 5000 per namespace
flow and tool graphs never loop back and run within a step budget
/recordings returns at most 1000 rows; other lists capped per route; REST offset uncapped (N-VOLUME)
a new key makes stored credentials and encrypted files unreadable (keep keys stable; §1.13)

Excludes saved telemetry headers when the endpoint moves host (unresolved, Q35 -> MODEL-GAP). A non-admin reaching any admin operand is in model.

an egress firewall; netguard guards web import, iCal feeds, extension http tools, notifications and Chromium, nothing else; admin-set URLs other than iCal feeds (model, speech, Fedora, IIIF import, rclone sources, IMAP, MQTT bridge, OIDC, telemetry, tunnel) are unguarded
a sandbox for Python code tools; audit hooks, rlimits and an optional network namespace only raise the bar; admin-written code; runs as the Lens user
integrity beyond HTTPS and the publisher for llama.cpp, cloudflared, pip installs and hf: models; catalog GGUF files are still checked (P-MODEL-CHECKSUM)

downstream_responsibilities: Put everything behind HTTPS before exposing it beyond one machine, and set server.secure_cookies: true there
Use docker-compose.prod.yml or an installer, never dev compose, and set unique secrets
Change the SurrealDB credential when SurrealDB runs as its own server
Outside the compose files, put a reverse proxy in front of the web app that sets X-Forwarded-For
List exactly the front hops in server.trusted_proxies or LENS_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOSTS
Enable TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS only behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-Host
List served hosts in server.allowed_hosts; never * on an exposed host
Set iiif.allowed_origins to trusted viewer sites
Keep ACCESS_SECRET_KEY and ARCHIVE_SECRET_KEY stable and backed up; rotate ACCESS_SECRET_KEY to cut every outstanding signed link
Back up the key separately from the data; prefer ARCHIVE_SECRET_KEY from outside the volume; protect backups like the data
Put the data volume on an encrypted disk
Treat the server log as secret until the first admin exists, and while mail is unset
Make only fully trusted people admins
Choose identity providers that verify emails
After a password change or suspected theft, revoke API tokens and app grants, or disable the account
List private networks in documents.web_networks or notifications.networks only on purpose
When sensors are on, firewall ports 1883 and 5514 or bind them to a private address
Give the chat-room bridge its own low-role account
Run workers only on trusted hosts; they hold the DB credential
Pick model and speech servers you trust with transcripts and audio
Run conversion where Chromium can keep its sandbox (non-root, user namespaces)
Enable another person's extension only when you trust its author
Escape exported text, RDF, IIIF metadata and assistant output for your own sink
Treat transcript text and MCP results as untrusted prompt input in your agents
Keep the IIIF cookie SameSite=None; Secure by serving IIIF over HTTPS
Verify webhook-signature on receipt; treat Slack and Discord target URLs as secrets
Keep logs that record request paths private when sensor push tokens are in use

known_misuse.pattern: Broad server.trusted_proxies (for example a whole LAN)
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Any host in it can claim any visitor address and open IP groups

known_misuse.pattern: An IP group for everything with no reverse proxy outside compose
known_misuse.instead: Add a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For

known_misuse.pattern: Pasting signed media links into chats or tickets
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Anyone with the link opens the media until it expires
known_misuse.instead: Share a revocable share link instead

known_misuse.pattern: Enabling a teammate's shared extension without reading it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Its http tool can send your readable data to its author's host

known_misuse.pattern: Turning on the chat-room bridge without its own account
known_misuse.why_unsafe: The room reads as the admin
known_misuse.instead: Give the bridge a low-role account

known_misuse.pattern: Making someone admin so they can write a Python tool
known_misuse.instead: Use prompt, graph or http tools

known_misuse.why_unsafe: Editors, and iCal feed redirects, can then reach those networks

known_misuse.pattern: Webhook push token in a URL that proxies log
known_misuse.why_unsafe: The token is a credential in the path

known_misuse.pattern: Pointing the assistant at a hosted model for sensitive archives

known_non_findings.reported_as: A signed link works without a session, or after sign-out or role loss
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers authz; symptom 'info-leak to a link holder'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The server issued the link through an allow-listed field (`media.LINK_KEYS`), to a principal who could read that path when it was issued, and it is within its expiry. A link minted from text people or models wrote is P-MEDIA-LINK, not this entry.
known_non_findings.suppression: The server issued the link through an allow-listed field (media.LINK_KEYS), to a principal who could read that path when it was issued, and it is within its expiry. A link minted from text people or models wrote is P-MEDIA-LINK, not this entry

known_non_findings.reported_as: A recording's description shows while its parts are closed
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers authz; symptom 'info-leak of description'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The field is the description, shown to someone who may see the page.
known_non_findings.suppression: The field is the description, shown to someone who may see the page

known_non_findings.reported_as: A logged-in device subscribes to # and reads other streams
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers optional; symptom 'info-leak between devices'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): Sensors on; the client holds a hub login or anonymous mode is on.
known_non_findings.suppression: Sensors on; the client holds a hub login or anonymous mode is on

known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers ingest; symptom 'missing sandbox flag'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): Running as root or without user namespaces; the `netguard` proxy is in the path.
known_non_findings.suppression: Running as root or without user namespaces; the netguard proxy is in the path

known_non_findings.reported_as: A scanner flags rdflib's XML parser
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers query; symptom 'XXE, billion laughs'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The input reaches RDF import, which refuses RDF/XML.
known_non_findings.suppression: The input reaches RDF import, which refuses RDF/XML

known_non_findings.reported_as: The setup code or a sign-in link appears in the server log
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers identity; symptom 'info-leak to log readers'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): Read from the log by someone with log access.
known_non_findings.suppression: Read from the log by someone with log access

open_questions.claim: Q1: `iiif.allowed_origins` defaults to `["*"]`, and the IIIF cookie is `SameSite=None`. Is that default supported on an exposed host?
open_questions.proposed: no; on an exposed host the operator lists trusted viewer origins, and a report that needs `*` routes `OUT-OF-MODEL: non-default-build`. Alternative: supported, and §1.12 disclaims that any site can get an IIIF token for a person signed in to IIIF.

open_questions.claim: Q2: Outside the compose files (web app alone, `install.sh`, NAS packages, Proxmox), is IP-group and throttle trust promised as shipped, or only behind a reverse proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-For`?
open_questions.proposed: each shipped variant promises a correct trusted-proxy chain by default, as the compose files do; a shipped variant that makes visitors share one address, or lets them claim one, is `VALID` under P-IPGROUP or P-THROTTLE. A chain the operator builds stays N-XFF.

open_questions.claim: Q3: Do a password change, a reset or "remove all passkeys" end API tokens, app grants and IIIF cookies?
open_questions.proposed: no; disclaim. Disabling the account ends them all.

open_questions.claim: Q4: Is the 168-hour web session sliding (reset on each refresh) or absolute?
open_questions.proposed: sliding; no absolute cap is promised.

open_questions.claim: Q5: Anonymous `refresh`, `ticket`, `password/forgot`, `passkey/options`, `oauth/token` and short-share-code guesses are unthrottled; counters are per process and reset on restart; each API process has its own setup code unless `LENS_SETUP_CODE` is set; expiry uses wall-clock time. Disclaim all of these?
open_questions.proposed: yes. These are volume attacks on secrets of 58 bits or more.

open_questions.claim: Q6: Existence leaks: the passkey 404, external-login messages that echo an email, anonymous 401 versus 404, and sequential ids. Disclaim?
open_questions.proposed: yes, correctness-only. Only password sign-in and signed-in 404s promise non-disclosure.

open_questions.claim: Q7: A share token (`?s=`) works on the audio, video, frames and page API routes, not only the player and embed. By design?
open_questions.proposed: yes; it grants viewer on that one recording on any route that takes `s`.

open_questions.claim: Q8: Each handler checks its own role, with no central policy. Is that the contract for the roughly 370 routes read by gate only? Is the public surface just the auth, OAuth, passkey, external-login, sensor-push, `/public`, IIIF, embed and share routes? Do role changes apply on the next request? Is `proxy.ts` only a page gate?
open_questions.proposed: yes to all. A route that skips its check breaks P-NS-ISOLATION.

open_questions.claim: Q9: All namespaces share one database and credential. Are worker hosts and credential holders trusted peers, so a DB-level compromise voids isolation by design?
open_questions.proposed: yes; disclaim.

open_questions.claim: Q10: Share links survive the creator losing their role. Report links sign media for every recording in the page. Signed links outlive role removal and moves. By design?
open_questions.proposed: yes; disclaim. Revoke shares, or rotate `ACCESS_SECRET_KEY`.

open_questions.claim: Q11: Saved assistant answers are not re-filtered after access is lost; only cited passages are. Accept, limited to text the same person already saw?
open_questions.proposed: yes; correctness-only.

open_questions.claim: Q12: Delete commits rows atomically and removes files after. Move, merge, graph undo and RDF import are stepwise. Job steps run at least once and are not rolled back. Disclaim, provided partial state never widens access?
open_questions.proposed: yes; partial state is possible after a crash.

open_questions.claim: Q13: `docs/mcp.md` opens "Everything it can do only reads", yet three write tools exist. Is the "Every tool reads, except" paragraph the contract? Are tokens naming no server accepted at `/mcp` by design?
open_questions.proposed: yes to both; write tools need write scope and the editor role.

open_questions.claim: Q14: `secret.key` sits in `data_dir` with the sealed rows and backups. Does "encrypted at rest" protect only against a database-only or export-only leak?
open_questions.proposed: yes; disclaim a stolen `data_dir` that holds the key.

open_questions.claim: Q15: Notification targets may use any port; the guard checks addresses only. By design?
open_questions.proposed: yes.

open_questions.claim: Q16: IIIF import holds media up to 4 GB in memory, rclone copies have no byte cap, and SPARQL has no time bound. Guarantee or disclaim?
open_questions.proposed: disclaim; admin-started. (Listener connection counts moved to N-VOLUME.)

open_questions.claim: Q17: Remote content (storage, mail, calendars, IIIF manifests, model replies) is untrusted data. Remote names become local paths only through hashes and `clean_name`. Symlinks inside `sources.local_roots` are followed. Confirm?
open_questions.proposed: yes to all.

open_questions.claim: Q18: Error text from admin-set servers (up to 300 characters of the reply, internal host names, a URL as typed) may reach the person whose action triggered the call. Accept?
open_questions.field: outputs (§1.8; YAML only, no JSON field)
open_questions.proposed: yes; credentials typed into a URL are the admin's choice.

open_questions.claim: Q19: Side-effect holes: optional extras fetch weights; plain `urllib` callers honour `HTTP(S)_PROXY`; the loopback guard proxy is usable by local processes during a capture; SPARQL sets a process-global flag; temp files live outside `data_dir`; the web app was not scanned. Is this the full list?
open_questions.proposed: yes; same-host processes are trusted.

open_questions.claim: Q20: Every subprocess takes an argument list with server-built paths, never a shell, and decoder memory bugs are upstream. Lens promises arguments, timeouts and process-group kills, not a sandbox. Is a conversion or capture that outlives its timeout, or leaves children alive after a kill (a print command that never finishes, a hung LibreOffice), a Lens defect?
open_questions.proposed: yes; claim P-CONVERT-TIMEOUT (every conversion and capture ends within its timeout, with its whole process group), correctness-only. Alternative: disclaim in N-DECODERS.

open_questions.claim: Q21: Lens passes no `-protocol_whitelist` to ffmpeg. If an upload (`.m3u8` playlist or concat file) makes ffmpeg read another local file or fetch a URL, is that a breach?
open_questions.proposed: yes, `VALID` under P-NO-INJECTION. Alternative: disclaim demuxer behaviour in §1.12.

open_questions.claim: Q22: docx XML is read whole; emails nest without a depth cap; some decoders lack a timeout; media duration is unbounded. Guarantee or disclaim?
open_questions.proposed: disclaim size, nesting and duration; a stuck job is requeued after `stale_minutes`. Timeouts themselves are Q20.

open_questions.claim: Q23: Any writer can use a `template` node in a custom node. Is the Jinja sandbox a security guarantee for that reach?
open_questions.proposed: yes; an escape there is `VALID` under P-NO-CODE.

open_questions.claim: Q24: Is stored text from a lower role running as script in another person's browser (notes, transcripts, a `javascript:` link in the notes editor, the player) a promised boundary? Do consumers outside Lens own escaping for exports and RDF?
open_questions.proposed: yes to both. Stored XSS inside the web app is `VALID`.

open_questions.claim: Q25: Cypher refuses nested repeats heuristically; one regex match cannot be stopped mid-way. Admin workflow regexes are unguarded. Is the 8-second budget a guarantee?
open_questions.proposed: a correctness-only guarantee; ReDoS past the heuristic is volume-class; admin regexes are trusted.

open_questions.claim: Q26: Prompt injection from content is disclaimed when it only changes the model's words or writes a note in a namespace the person can edit, and `VALID` only when it crosses the person's reads, approvals or role. What about injected text that makes an answer carry readable text to an attacker URL (a rendered image or link)?
open_questions.proposed: confirm the first part, including that `write_note` needs no approval. For the egress channel: answers must not fetch on render, so such a report is `VALID-HARDENING`. Alternative: disclaim it in N-PROMPT.

open_questions.claim: Q27: An extension's `effect: read` label is the author's word, and a shared `http` tool can send a user's readable data to the author's host. Does another person's tool run in my assistant only when an admin shared it or I enabled it, and can tool arguments change the `http` tool's host?
open_questions.proposed: claim P-EXT-SCOPE for tools too (another person's tool runs only when an admin shared it or I enabled it; arguments never change the host), security-critical. Alternative: disclaim, and enabling another person's extension is an act of trust.

open_questions.claim: Q28: The chat-room bridge answers as the admin when no account is set. Supported on an exposed instance?
open_questions.proposed: supported; the admin owns the choice.

open_questions.claim: Q29: Are the sensor limits (256 KB payload, 600 per minute, 64 KB syslog line) promises or tunables? Is an unauthenticated MQTT publish, with `mqtt_anonymous` off, a breach?
open_questions.proposed: tunables; the unauthenticated publish is `VALID` under P-SENSORS.

open_questions.claim: Q30: Cloudflare terminates TLS for tunnel traffic. Is it a trusted dependency? Is the quick `trycloudflare.com` address for real use?
open_questions.proposed: trusted; the quick address is for trying Lens.

open_questions.claim: Q31: `install.sh` on a headless host and the NAS packages listen on all interfaces over HTTP, and print a `?code=` setup URL. Supported only on a trusted LAN until HTTPS is set up?
open_questions.proposed: yes; the setup window relies on a code of about 72 bits and a private log. Until ratified such reports route `non-default-build (escalated)`.

open_questions.claim: Q32: Is the server log an operator-trusted channel, so setup codes and sign-in links there are by design, while stored source and model credentials never appear?
open_questions.proposed: yes.

open_questions.claim: Q33: Proxmox services run as root inside the unprivileged LXC; the SurrealDB container runs as root. Supported?
open_questions.proposed: yes; the container is the boundary.

open_questions.claim: Q34: Coverage and scope: not yet read per item are about 60 assistant read tools and 30 settings tools, per-role file parsers (SRT, VTT, JSON, OHMS XML), faces, voice and objects, pipeline and routine actions, and the frontend pages. `examples/`, `overrides/`, `ci/`, `prod-frontend-deploy.yml`, `tests/`, `watcher.py` and `commands/` are unsupported or inert. No vendored third-party source ships. The N/A matrix rows tagged with this question hold. Confirm, and complete the rest next revision?
open_questions.proposed: yes; treat the unread surface as **inferred** until then.

open_questions.claim: Q35: P-ADMIN-GUARD claims the documented guards on iCal feeds and the telemetry endpoint. Is it security-critical, and does moving the telemetry endpoint to another host also promise to drop the saved headers, so a collector's token never reaches a new host?
open_questions.proposed: security-critical for the iCal guard (a remote calendar's redirect is attacker-controlled); correctness-only for the telemetry checks; yes, the header drop is promised and joins P-ADMIN-GUARD.

open_questions.claim: Q36: Is every default exposure of the dev stack unsupported, or only its known secrets, `SURREAL_PASS=root` and the web port on all interfaces?
open_questions.proposed: only those; any other dev-stack port reachable beyond loopback (API, DB, Mailpit, MQTT, syslog) is a defect, fixed when found and claimed under P-HARDENED.

open_questions.claim: Q37: Confirm the tiers of the documented properties promoted in this revision: P-ACCESS-PARTS, P-BEARER-ONLY, P-FRAME, P-EXT-SCOPE and P-ADMIN-GUARD (security-critical); P-LIFETIMES, P-HARDENED, P-CHILD-SECRETS and P-REMOTE-NAMES (correctness-only).
open_questions.proposed: confirm as listed. This is an edge probe of documented claims.

open_questions.claim: Q38: With `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS` off and the default trusted proxies, can any request header choose the address that OAuth discovery, the passkey origin or the external-login redirect names?
open_questions.proposed: no; claim it, security-critical, from docs/authentication.md "anyone could choose the address". Alternative: disclaim.

open_questions.claim: Q39: Can a token minted while its grant or API token is being revoked outlive the revocation?
open_questions.proposed: no; claim it as part of P-AUTH-REQ ("its tokens stop working at once").

open_questions.claim: Q40: Is the post-sign-in `next` target (external login, sign-in links) limited to same-origin paths?
open_questions.proposed: yes; claim it, correctness-only. Alternative: disclaim open redirects.

open_questions.claim: Q41: Can a request by anyone but a pending sign-in link's owner or an admin (for example an anonymous "lost your passkey" email) cancel that link?
open_questions.proposed: no; claim it, correctness-only.

open_questions.claim: Q42: Setup-code guesses are unthrottled. Add the setup routes to N-THROTTLE-SCOPE (resting on the code's entropy), or throttle them?
open_questions.proposed: disclaim; the code is about 72 bits and lives only until the first admin exists.

open_questions.claim: Q43: Beyond IMAP (P-REMOTE-NAMES), is remote content from rclone sources, iCal feeds and IIIF imports served only under the identity it was fetched for?
open_questions.proposed: yes; claim it, correctness-only.

open_questions.claim: Q44: Are released images built only from clean CI checkouts, so host-local files such as `.env.local` cannot enter a layer?
open_questions.proposed: yes for released packages; a local build from a working tree is dev-only.

open_questions.claim: Q45: §1.9: are SurrealDB, Next.js and NextAuth, PyJWT, `webauthn`, `cryptography`, rclone and the stdlib clients upstream-owned as listed, and is the build, lint and codegen toolchain out of every running service?
open_questions.field: dependencies (§1.9; YAML only, no JSON field)
open_questions.proposed: yes to both; a toolchain advisory is in model only when the affected code ships in an image.

open_questions.claim: Q46: Meta: the backtest found candidate known non-findings for OIDC nonce or ID-token checks (N-OIDC), phishing through open app registration (N-OAUTH-CLIENT), and audit-log tamper evidence (N-AUDIT), but each rests on one synthesized report. Do you actually receive these reports often enough to list them in §1.15?
open_questions.proposed: only list the ones you have seen at least twice; until then they route `BY-DESIGN: property-disclaimed` through §1.12.

open_questions.claim: Q47: Do MCP tool arguments (offsets, page sizes) promise the same maximums as the REST search API, for example a 10,000 cap on `get_entity`'s mentions offset?
open_questions.proposed: yes; MCP tools share the search maximums, and a tool argument past them is refused.
